question.text:
The motion of a particle traveling along the x-axis is described by a velocity-time graph. At t = 0 s, the position of the particle is x = 10 m.

The velocity varies with time as follows:
• From t = 0 s to t = 2 s, velocity increases linearly from 0 m/s to 4 m/s.
• From t = 2 s to t = 8 s, velocity decreases linearly from 4 m/s to −8 m/s (crossing 0 m/s at t = 4 s).
• From t = 8 s to t = 12 s, velocity is constant at −8 m/s.
• From t = 12 s to t = 16 s, velocity increases linearly from −8 m/s to 0 m/s.

Answer the following questions based on this motion:

parts.label: a
parts.asks: Draw the position-time (x versus t) graph of the particle from t = 0 s to t = 16 s.

parts.label: b
parts.asks: Calculate both the average velocity and the average speed for the entire duration of the motion (from t = 0 s to t = 16 s).

parts.label: c
parts.asks: Determine the average acceleration of the particle in the time span between t = 2 s and t = 8 s.

conditions: at t = 0 s, position x = 10 m
total time interval is from t = 0 s to t = 16 s

figure.description: A velocity-time (v-t) graph where the vertical axis represents velocity v in m/s with marked values −8, 0, 4, and the horizontal axis represents time t in seconds with marked points 2, 4, 8, 12, 16. The plot starts at (0, 0), rises to (2, 4), goes down straight through (4, 0) to (8, −8), runs horizontally from (8, −8) to (12, −8), and then rises linearly to (16, 0).

solution.approach: Use the area under the velocity-time graph in each segment to build the x-coordinate step by step, then use total displacement and total distance for the averages.

steps.text: Read the graph in five straight segments: 0 to 2 s (v from 0 to 4), 2 to 4 s (v from 4 to 0), 4 to 8 s (v from 0 to −8), 8 to 12 s (v constant at −8), 12 to 16 s (v from −8 to 0).
Add each area to the running x-coordinate, starting from x = 10 m at t = 0.
Average velocity over the whole journey is the total displacement divided by the total time.
Average speed is the total distance travelled, the sum of the sizes of each segment's area, divided by the total time.
Average acceleration between t = 2 s and t = 8 s is the change in velocity divided by the change in time, read from the graph.

final_answer.value: (a) x goes 10→14→18→2→−30→−46 m at t=0,2,4,8,12,16 s; (b) average velocity = −3.5 m/s, average speed = 4.5 m/s; (c) average acceleration = −2 m/s²

common_mistakes.text: Using the total distance instead of the total displacement in the average velocity formula gives 72/16 = 4.5 m/s for both average velocity and average speed.
Dividing the velocity change by the total time 8 s instead of by the 6 s interval from t = 2 s to t = 8 s gives -1.5 m/s2 instead of -2 m/s2.
